title: Compound Tenses
description: Master haber + past participle to form perfect tenses: present perfect, past perfect, and future perfect.

grammar.title: Present Perfect
grammar.content:
Present Perfect = haber (present) + past participle

Formation:
He hablado (I have spoken)
Has comido (You have eaten)
Ha vivido (He/She has lived)
Hemos terminado (We have finished)
Han llegado (They have arrived)

Past participles:
-AR verbs → -ado (hablado, comido, vivido)
-ER/-IR verbs → -ido (tenido, hecho, dicho)

Irregular past participles:
hacer → hecho
decir → dicho
ver → visto
escribir → escrito
leer → leido
abrir → abierto
cerrar → cerrado
romper → roto
morir → muerto
poner → puesto
volver → vuelto
resolver → resuelto
cubrir → cubierto
descubrir → descubierto
imprimir → impreso

Uses:
1. Actions that happened at an unspecified time:
He estado en Espana tres veces. (I have been in Spain three times.)

2. Actions that started in the past and continue to present:
He vivido aqui desde 2010. (I have lived here since 2010.)

3. Actions just completed:
Acabo de llegar. (I have just arrived.)
examples: He terminado la tarea. (I have finished the homework.)
Hemos comido en ese restaurante antes. (We have eaten at that restaurant before.)
Nunca he ido a Mexico. (I have never been to Mexico.)
Ya he leido el libro. (I have already read the book.)

grammar.title: Past Perfect and Future Perfect
grammar.content:
PAST PERFECT (Pluscuamperfecto):
Haber (imperfect) + past participle

Habia hablado (I had spoken)
Habias comido (You had eaten)
Habia vivido (He/She had lived)
Habianos terminado (We had finished)
Habian llegado (They had arrived)

Uses: An action that happened BEFORE another past action:
Cuando llegue, el ya se habia ido. (When I arrived, he had already left.)

FUTURE PERFECT:
Habra + past participle

Habre terminado para manana. (I will have finished by tomorrow.)
Para 2030, habre viajado por 50 paises. (By 2030, I will have traveled to 50 countries.)

CONDITIONAL PERFECT:
Habria + past participle

Habria venido si me hubieras avisado. (I would have come if you had warned me.)
examples: Cuando llegue, ella ya habia salido. (When I arrived, she had already left.)
Si hubiera estudiado, habria aprobado. (If I had studied, I would have passed.)
Para el ano que viene, habre aprendido espanol. (By next year, I will have learned Spanish.)
Habria venido si me hubieras invitado. (I would have come if you had invited me.)

grammar.title: Subjunctive in Compound Tenses
grammar.content:
PRESENT PERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE:
Haya + past participle

Haya hablado (I have spoken)
Hayas comido (You have eaten)
Haya vivido (He/She has lived)
Hayamos terminado (We have finished)
Hayan llegado (They have arrived)

Uses: After expressions of doubt/will in present:
Dudo que haya llegado. (I doubt he has arrived.)
Espero que hayas terminado. (I hope you have finished.)

PAST PERFECT SUBJUNCTIVE:
Hubiera/Hubiese + past participle

Uses: Unreal past conditions/wishes:
Si hubiera sabido, te hubiera avisado. (If I had known, I would have warned you.)
Ojalia hubiera estudiado mas. (I wish I had studied more.)

Sequence of tenses with subjunctive:
MAIN CLAUSE → SUBJUNCTIVE CLAUSE
Present/Future → Present Perfect
Past → Past Perfect

Espero que hayas venido (present/future main)
Esperaba que hubieras venido (past main)
examples: Dudo que haya terminado. (I doubt he has finished.)
Es probable que haya llovido. (It's probable that it has rained.)
Si hubiera llegado a tiempo, me hubiera tocado. (If I had arrived on time, it would have been my turn.)
No crei que hubieras hecho la tarea. (I didn't think you had done the homework.)

pronunciation.title: Compound Tense Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Key pronunciations:

he = eh
has = ahs
ha = ah
hemos = EH-mohs
han = ahn

habia = ah-BEE-ah
habias = ah-BEE-ahs
habia = ah-BEE-ah
habamos = ah-BAH-mohs
habian = ah-BEE-ahn

Past participles:
hablado = ah-BLAH-doh
comido = koh-MEE-doh
vivido = bee-BEE-doh
hecho = EH-choh
dicho = DEE-choh
visto = BEES-toh

Irregulars:
roto = ROH-toh
muerto = MWEHR-toh
abierto = ah-BYEHR-toh
cubierto = koo-BYEHR-toh
puesto = PWEHS-toh
resuelto = reh-SWEHL-toh

exercises.question: What is the present perfect of 'hablar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: Present perfect = he + past participle. 'He hablado' = I have spoken.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ya ___ terminado la tarea. (I have already finished the homework.)'
exercises.explanation: He terminado = I have finished. 'Ya' (already) indicates present perfect.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I have never been to Mexico'?
exercises.explanation: 'Nunca he ido a Mexico' = I have never been to Mexico. Present perfect with 'nunca'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Cuando llegue, el ya se ___ ido. (When I arrived, he had already left.)'
exercises.explanation: Se habia ido = he had left. Past perfect (habia + past participle) for action before another past action.

exercises.question: What is the past participle of 'hacer'?
exercises.explanation: Hecho is the irregular past participle of hacer. Many -er verbs have irregular participles.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Es probable que ___ llovido. (It's probable that it has rained.)'
exercises.explanation: Haya llovido = it has rained (present perfect subjunctive). After 'es probable que', use subjunctive.

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I would have come if you had invited me'?
options: Habria venido si me hubieras invitado
exercises.explanation: 'Habria venido si me hubieras invitado' uses conditional perfect + past perfect subjunctive.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Para manana, ___ terminado el proyecto. (By tomorrow, I will have finished the project.)'
exercises.explanation: Habre terminado = I will have finished. Future perfect for action completed before a future time.

exercises.question: What is the past participle of 'romper'?
exercises.explanation: Roto is the irregular past participle of romper (to break).

exercises.question: Complete: 'Dudo que ___ terminado. (I doubt he has finished.)'
exercises.explanation: Haya terminado = he has finished (present perfect subjunctive). After 'dudo que', use subjunctive.
